title: Light Computer Light Tools — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Light tools are the instruments that shape, split, steer, and measure light — the screwdrivers and calipers of the photonic workshop. Lenses focus, beam splitters divide, spatial light modulators sculpt wavefronts pixel by pixel, and interferometers measure to fractions of a wavelength. Manon's order centers the light computer on these tools: the machine is as much an instrument as a computer, and its tools are first-class pieces with their own database.

title: Light Computer Light Tools — Lenses, mirrors, and prisms
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. The classics: lenses focus and collimate (focal length from the lensmaker's equation), mirrors fold paths without loss (dielectric mirrors reflect over 99.9 percent), prisms and gratings split wavelengths. These are centuries-old, perfected tools — and still the fastest way to do a Fourier transform: a lens performs an exact 2D Fourier transform of the light at its focal plane, at the speed of light, with zero power. The light computer's math coprocessor is literally a lens.

title: Light Computer Light Tools — Beam splitters and combiners
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Beam splitters divide one beam into two (50/50 cubes and plates are the standard), and run backward they combine. Polarizing splitters separate by polarization; dichroic splitters by color. Splitters are the fan-out of optical logic: one signal becomes many, or many interfere into one. Their spec is the split ratio tolerance and the loss — typically a few percent — and cascades of them build interferometric logic networks.

title: Light Computer Light Tools — Spatial light modulators
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. A spatial light modulator (SLM) is a display for light: typically a liquid-crystal panel with millions of pixels, each setting the phase or amplitude of the light passing through. SLMs sculpt arbitrary wavefronts — holograms, lens patterns, vortex beams — under software control. They are the light tool with the most leverage: one SLM replaces rooms of fixed optics, and updating the pattern reprograms the instrument in milliseconds.

title: Light Computer Light Tools — Holography as optical memory and processing
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Holograms store information as interference patterns in a medium (photographic plates historically, photorefractive crystals and polymers now). A single hologram stores a whole image; stacked holograms store thousands of pages in the same volume — holographic data storage is real, researched technology. For computing, holograms are fixed optical programs: shine the input through and the output is the transformed light. They are the light computer's read-only memory.

title: Light Computer Light Tools — Interferometers: measurement to a fraction of a wavelength
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Interferometers split light, send it down two paths, and recombine it: the interference reveals path differences far below a wavelength. Michelson, Mach-Zehnder, and Fabry-Perot designs are the standards; LIGO is a Michelson interferometer measuring 10^-19 metre displacements. In the light computer, interferometers are both tools (aligning and calibrating the machine) and logic (interferometric gates compute by interference). Precision is the product.

title: Light Computer Light Tools — Optical tweezers and light-matter handling
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Focused laser beams trap and move microscopic objects — optical tweezers, Nobel-recognized in 2018. In the light computer's workshop, tweezers position components, hold samples in measurement beams, and could even arrange plasma-adjacent structures. The tool piece covers trap stiffness, positioning accuracy (nanometres), and the force calibration. Light as a hand: the most delicate tweezers ever built.

title: Light Computer Light Tools — The light-tool workshop in the full stack
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Light tools serve both construction and operation: they build the machine (alignment, calibration), program it (SLM patterns, holograms), and verify it (interferometry, spectroscopy). The workshop piece is the lab around the computer — and per Manon's order, it is a first-class citizen, not an accessory. Beginner exercise: compute a lens's Fourier spot size for 1550-nm light and a 10-cm focal length (about 20 microns per unit spatial frequency) — and you have sized an optical processor.
